question: Where can machine learning most productively improve approximate liquid-state theories without discarding their physical structure and macroscopic efficiency?

key_findings.claim: The perspective identifies approximate closures and expensive iterative solution of the Ornstein--Zernike equation as natural targets for learned bridge functions and input-to-solution surrogates.
key_findings.evidence: It traces closure error to the analytically inaccessible bridge function, reviews neural closures trained from simulations, and contrasts PINN-style equation fitting with probabilistic emulators that expose uncertainty.

key_findings.claim: Classical density-functional theory offers a more general functional-learning route for inhomogeneous fluids, because learned one-body functionals can retain variational and thermodynamic constraints.
key_findings.evidence: The review connects integral equations and cDFT through functional calculus and summarizes learned free-energy, direct-correlation, and external-potential mappings, including extrapolation beyond some training conditions.

key_findings.claim: The authors argue that dimensionality reduction, Bayesian uncertainty, and active functional learning are needed for trustworthy extrapolation in high-dimensional molecular spaces.
key_findings.evidence: The proposed workflow uses predictive-error probabilities to request new simulations, while the perspective recommends active subspaces or low-dimensional summary coordinates and calibrated predictive intervals.

anchors.section: Active functional learning with error control

method.core_idea: Organize existing ML interventions around the equations, closures, and functionals of liquid-state theory, then propose uncertainty-aware functional learning as the next step.
method.mechanism: Review integral-equation and cDFT formalisms, locate their approximation and compute bottlenecks, compare learned closures and functionals, and outline active-learning loops that add simulation data when posterior error is too large.
assumptions: Simulation or scattering data adequately cover the relevant thermodynamic and interaction regimes.
Physical functional structure constrains learning enough to improve transfer beyond black-box surrogates.
Probabilistic emulator uncertainty remains calibrated under the intended extrapolations.

techniques.role: Approximates bridge functions or maps potentials and densities to correlations.
Learns cDFT quantities while retaining variational relationships.
Uses uncertainty to select new molecular simulations and control predictive error.

limitations: The article is a perspective and does not conduct a common benchmark across the reviewed methods.
Training labels ultimately come from simulations or experiments whose cost and model bias remain.
Uncertainty calibration and physical consistency can deteriorate far from training states.
Mixtures, molecular orientation, long-range interactions, and phase transitions greatly expand the functional input space.
failure_modes: A learned closure can violate thermodynamic consistency or make the OZ iteration diverge.
An emulator may report overconfident predictions under a new potential or phase.
Dimension reduction can discard rare coordinates that govern phase behavior.
reusable_insights: Learn corrections to a known physical approximation when possible, rather than relearning the entire map.
Functional derivatives and sum rules create stronger tests than pointwise prediction error alone.
Active learning is most useful when its uncertainty signal is checked for coverage, not merely produced.
open_questions: Which liquid-state constraints should be enforced architecturally versus through loss penalties?
Can learned functionals transfer across mixtures, molecular geometries, and phase boundaries?
What benchmark jointly measures structure, thermodynamics, convergence, uncertainty coverage, and simulation savings?

competitive_landscape.title: Machine learnt approximations to the bridge function yield improved closures for the Ornstein-Zernike equation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct learned-closure approach reviewed by the perspective.
competitive_landscape.difference: Goodall and Lee build and test a specific neural bridge-function closure; the target synthesizes several liquid-theory routes and emphasizes future uncertainty-aware integration.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine-learning free-energy functionals using density profiles from simulations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct functional-learning implementation for Lennard-Jones fluids.
competitive_landscape.difference: Cats et al. empirically regress a non-mean-field free-energy contribution and audit derived observables; the target is a broader perspective spanning closures, structure-centered models, and cDFT.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural functional theory for inhomogeneous fluids: Fundamentals and applications
competitive_landscape.difference: Sammüller et al. learn a density-to-direct-correlation functional and validate derivatives, sum rules, and self-consistent profiles; the target mainly frames such work and proposes active uncertainty control.

novelty_assessment: This is a timely perspective rather than an original algorithm. Its value is the unified map from liquid-state equations to ML opportunities and the explicit case for uncertainty-aware active functional learning; most concrete methods are credited to prior work.
reviewer_notes: Read all 25 extracted pages, including the OCR-recovered final schematic. Findings are attributed as synthesis/proposals, not new experimental results. Direct primary arXiv competitors checked on 2026-08-23.
